stemMd: A botanist argues that seedlings grow poorly in one plot because its soil lacks a mineral. Which result would most strongly support the explanation?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Seedlings in a distant garden grow well.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The mineral is sold at garden centers.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The plot receives visitors every week.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Adding only that mineral to randomly selected sections improves growth relative to untreated sections of the same plot.

explanationMd: A controlled intervention that changes only the suspected factor directly tests the causal claim. Random allocation and a same-plot comparison reduce the chance that location or other soil differences explain the improvement.

distractorRationale.a: The distant garden differs in many uncontrolled ways.
distractorRationale.c: Availability does not show a growth effect.
distractorRationale.d: Visitor frequency does not test the mineral hypothesis.
distractorRationale.b: Leaf color alone does not isolate the deficiency.
